training_data_summary: Three-stage lineage, all verified against primary sources. (1) Pretraining: microsoft/deberta-v3-large on the RoBERTa-style corpus (Wikipedia, BookCorpus, CC-News, Stories, OpenWebText) per arXiv 2111.09543 Appendix A.2; no Twitter or emotion dataset is named. (2) Intermediate checkpoint: MoritzLaurer/deberta-v3-large-zeroshot-v2.0 (non-'-c'). Its card lists Mixtral-8x7B synthetic classification data, MNLI, FEVER-NLI, ANLI, WANLI, LingNLI, and 'all datasets in [pinned datasets_overview.csv] where used_in_v1.1==True'. In that pinned CSV the row 'emotion6_twitter' (dataset_link https://huggingface.co/datasets/dair-ai/emotion, paper D18-1404) is used_in_v1.0=TRUE, used_in_v1.1=TRUE. The card states the released non-'-c' model is the 'final run including up to 500 training data points per class from each of the 28 datasets', and 'emotiondair (6)' is one of the 28 (macro-F1 0.484 zero-shot -> 0.688 in the released run). Public code shows dair-ai/emotion train+validation were pooled (dedup, cap 10,000/label) with the test split kept separate, reformulated as NLI hypotheses 'This example tweet expresses the emotion: X'; the v2 training notebook loads a private pool 'MoritzLaurer/dataset_train_nli' whose saved output shows an 'emotiondair' subset of 10,344 NLI rows, and with heldout='none' nothing is removed. The '-c' variant (MNLI + FEVER + Mixtral synthetic) has no emotion data, but PrismNLI did not use it. (3) Final fine-tuning: 515,186 synthetic binary-NLI (entailment/not_entailment) pairs from Jaehun/PrismNLI, generated by Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct via Prismatic Synthesis seeded from WANLI (paper: 103k seeds; dataset card says 94k, which appears to be a copy-paste error from the PrismMath/OpenR1-Math description), decontaminated (10-gram + LLM paraphrase detection) only against the 8 NLI test benchmarks in Table 4. No emotion data is added at this stage, but fine-tuning from an emotion-exposed checkpoint does not remove the prior exposure. Note the PrismNLI-0.4B card's YAML `base_model` lists microsoft/deberta-v3-large, understating the lineage relative to its own prose.
published_dair_emotion_numbers: None for PrismNLI-0.4B. The model card and paper (arXiv 2505.20161) report only NLI benchmarks (HANS, WNLI, ANLI r1-r3, Diagnostics, BigBench, Control; PrismNLI-0.4B avg 82.88); full-text search of the arXiv HTML returns zero hits for 'emotion' or 'dair'. Third-party checks re-run: the BTZSC benchmark (arXiv 2603.11991, by Ilias Aarab) HTML contains 'emotion' and 'dair' but no occurrence of 'prism'; the AryanPakdel/text-classification-benchmark README (main and master, both HTTP 200) mentions 'emotion' 11 times but 'prism' zero times. For the starting checkpoint only: MoritzLaurer/deberta-v3-large-zeroshot-v2.0 card, row 'emotiondair (6)', column 'deberta-v3-large-zeroshot-v2.0 (fewshot)': macro-F1 0.484 in the pure zero-shot run and 0.688 in the released run that includes emotion training data; the '-c' variant column reports 0.499; facebook/bart-large-mnli 0.455 (https://huggingface.co/MoritzLaurer/deberta-v3-large-zeroshot-v2.0).
caveats: VERIFICATION RESULT: every one of the 15 quotes was re-fetched and found verbatim in its cited source (modulo removed line-wraps, PDF hyphenation 'combi- nation', and explicitly marked '...' elisions in the three notebook quotes). The verdict 'explicit evidence of training exposure' is justified: the PrismNLI card explicitly names its initialisation checkpoint, that checkpoint's card explicitly names the pinned CSV, the CSV explicitly lists dair-ai/emotion as used, and the card explicitly says the released run included training data from each of the 28 eval datasets including emotiondair. It is not overstated, provided the reader understands the exposure is to the train/validation splits via inherited weights, not to the test split and not via PrismNLI's own data. Corrections/additions made: (1) The dataset card's '94k' WANLI seed count conflicts with the paper's '103k' for WANLI; 94k is the paper's OpenR1-Math seed count, and the same card also says 'The dataset consists of 1M math problem-solution pairs', so the card contains copy-paste errors from PrismMath. The original summary's '94k-103k seeds' glossed over this; it is now flagged. (2) The original attributed the 'up to 500 training data points per class' cap to the card only; on inspection the public synth_train_eval.ipynb contains no code implementing that cap, and its saved output shows the private pool holds 10,344 'emotiondair' NLI rows (multiple hypotheses per text, so the unique-text count cannot be inferred). The 500-per-class figure therefore remains an author statement unverifiable against public artefacts. (3) Added the verified fact that the v2 notebook as committed sets ONLY_COMMERCIALLY_FRIENDLY_DATA = False and filters only 'mixtral_small_zeroshot' from the pool. (4) Confirmed the CSV header so that the TRUE,TRUE columns are unambiguously used_in_v1.0 and used_in_v1.1 (the original only mentioned v1.1). (5) Confirmed that DeBERTa-v3 paper text contains neither 'twitter' nor 'emotion'. (6) Confirmed third-party negatives (BTZSC and AryanPakdel) directly rather than relying on the prior search. Remaining caveats carried over unchanged: (a) exposure is inherited via the starting checkpoint; the PrismNLI paper never mentions this initialisation (its experiments start from raw DeBERTa-v3-large). (b) base_model metadata on the PrismNLI-0.4B card understates the lineage. (c) 'MoritzLaurer/dataset_train_nli' is private, so the exact emotion examples used cannot be inspected. (d) The claim 'No model was trained on test data' is an author assertion (unverifiable), consistent with the public v1 code that holds out the 2,000-example test split. (e) Whether the Hub v2.0 weights equal the 'fewshot' final run is inferred from the card's description and the notebook id 'deberta-v3-large-zeroshot-v2.0-2024-03-20-21-16'. (f) 515K-example PrismNLI fine-tuning may attenuate but does not erase prior exposure; this is a lineage-contamination finding, not a memorisation measurement. (g) Undocumented, unquantified possibility of tweets in DeBERTa pretraining corpora.

We built our training pipeline using 100% human-labeled, real-world public datasets across:
- Support Triage & Intents: Real customer service conversations, banking intents, and ticket routing queues.
- Inference & Fact Checking: Premise-hypothesis pairs, fact verification, and contradiction checks.
- Content Safety: Human consensus labels for toxic remarks, harassment, and severe abuse.
- Security & Guardrails: Real jailbreak prompts and prompt injection attacks.
- Rubrics & Quality: Multi-axis human rubric ratings for helpfulness, complexity, and correctness.
- Multi-Turn Trajectories: SaaS sales and support interactions with verified final outcomes.

To stop the model from taking shortcuts, our data pipeline dynamically shuffles option orders, paraphrases questions, alternates between raw text and nested JSON states, and injects random distractor questions.
